task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 -- design the fix for ISS-0426. Follow WF-02 Step 1's design procedure as WF-03 Step 2 directs. Produce a design artefact under lib/letflow/design/ (suggested name iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md); design only, NO implementation code.

READ ISSUE-FIXER's Step 1 diagnosis FIRST (artifacts_in[0], result.summary) -- it is the evidence base for this design and it contains the enumeration, the root-cause mechanism, and an options assessment. Per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1 its factual claims are checkable and may be wrong: verify the ones your design depends on (in particular the two-group split of the lua tests and the claim that all wasm-side wall-clock-sensitive tests are ALREADY tagged :wasm_hang) rather than inheriting them.

THE ESTABLISHED ROOT CAUSE, in mechanism terms: Executor.execute_with_manifest/3 races Task.yield(timeout_ms) against wall-clock time. handle_yield_result(nil, ...) fires when no reply arrived in time, which measures SCHEDULER AVAILABILITY for the child task and the calling process -- not Lua execution time. Under 6-way partitioning on 16 cores, six BEAM nodes oversubscribe the cores ~6x, so a microsecond-scale task can sit unscheduled past a 5000ms budget. The diagnosis splits the lua tests into two groups that need DIFFERENT treatment:
  GROUP 1 (~10 tests incl. the filed failure at executor_test.exs:983): a generous timeout_ms: 5_000 wrapped around trivial real work, where the timeout is incidental scaffolding and ANY timeout outcome is a wrong-branch failure. ORCH has independently confirmed this reading for AC7 at line 983: that test asserts a SCRIPT_ERROR from integer division by zero; the 5000ms budget is not the property under test at all.
  GROUP 2 (~9 tests): a tight budget where the race IS the property under test -- these legitimately assert timeout behaviour and must keep doing so.

ISSUE-FIXER's recommendation, which you may adopt, refine, or reject with stated reasoning: option (c) restructure for GROUP 1, option (a) tag-and-isolate (mirroring the :wasm_hang precedent in test/test_helper.exs and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex) for GROUP 2. Option (b) raise-the-budget alone is NOT recommended and the diagnosis gives the reason: config/test.exs:187's own history shows this budget already raised twice (200 -> 1500 -> 5000ms) and exceeded again both times. Note also the diagnosis's finding that config/test.exs:187 is DEAD CODE for the filed failure, because AC7 pins its own timeout_ms: 5_000 literal and never falls through to config -- so any design leaning on the config value must say how the pinned literals are reached.

HARD CONSTRAINTS your design must satisfy and state that it satisfies:
  1. (ISS-0426 AC4) Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor's PRODUCTION wall-clock kill semantics unchanged -- no production timeout constant raised or removed, config/config.exs:17's 5_000 untouched. It is REQ-155's LUA-10 layer-2 security control against untrusted tenant scripts. A design that relaxes it to fix a test environment problem is rejected outright.
  2. (ISS-0426 AC5) If your design tags/partitions rather than rewrites, the tagging MUST be wired into test/test_helper.exs AND mix letflow.check.test the same way wasm_hang already is, so a plain `mix test` and CI both stay correct. Read how :wasm_hang does it (test_helper.exs:19-33's ExUnit.start(exclude: ...) and letflow.check.test.ex's run_wasm_hang_tests/0 subprocess) and mirror the shape.
  3. (ISS-0426 AC3) The suite must still pass SERIALLY under plain `mix test`. Do not trade serial correctness for parallel safety.
  4. GROUP 2's tests must still genuinely prove the timeout behaviour they exist to prove. A restructure that makes a timeout test unable to fail is a worse defect than the flake.

SCOPE BOUNDARY -- CONCURRENT RUN. WF03-ISS0418-20260902 is live on another host implementing the OQ-5 WASM concurrency cap and owns lib/letflow/engine/wasm, test/letflow/engine/wasm/{call_timeout,plugin_handler,host_api_write}_test.exs, and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex. Your design may READ all of these. It must NOT require editing the three wasm test files. lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex is a CONTESTED file: if AC5 forces a change there, design the change as a MINIMAL, ADDITIVE one (a new isolated-subprocess invocation alongside the existing wasm_hang one, not a restructure of it) and flag the contention explicitly in your design's own risks section so ORCH can sequence the merge against ISS-0418.

ALSO NOTE, and design around: ISSUE-FIXER could NOT reproduce the failure with a cheaper single-file contention probe (it ran up to 24 OS-level CPU burners plus 8x6 concentrated AC7-only runs, all clean) and reported that honestly as a negative rather than disproof -- the real filed observation came from a full 6-way partitioned suite run. ISS-0426's AC6 requires the fix be shown to work across at least two repeated end-to-end runs. So your design should, where it can, prefer a fix whose correctness is STRUCTURALLY evident (the failure branch is removed or made unreachable) over one that can only be validated statistically by not-flaking -- because a probabilistic fix is very expensive to demonstrate here. State in the design how a validator can tell your fix works WITHOUT needing to first reproduce a flake that resists reproduction.

Deliverable: the design document, plus a complete handoff (PASS/FAIL, artifacts_out naming the design path, next_action routing to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR). Commit the design and your handoff to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902.

result.summary:
Design written to lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md. Verified ISSUE-FIXER's mechanism and both enumeration claims (WASM-side already tagged :wasm_hang -- confirmed correct; the lua two-group split -- confirmed real but REFINED: found 5 more Group-1-shaped call sites the diagnosis's own enumeration omitted, all in the REQ-154 instruction-budget describe block, same 'generous 5000ms scaffolding wrapping a fast/expected-non-timeout outcome' shape as AC7 -- and found 2 tests (lines 656/887) that are internally MIXED, containing both a Group-1-shaped and a genuinely-racing Group-2-shaped execute_with_manifest call in the same test body, which the diagnosis's enumeration did not flag as a structural wrinkle). Also found and flagged a stale comment (executor_test.exs:320 says config/test.exs sets '200ms'; the actual value is 5000 -- matches ISSUE-FIXER's own correct citation, so this is a pre-existing drift in the test file's own comment, not a disagreement with the diagnosis) for ELIXIR-DEV to correct as a drive-by fix.

Design per group: GROUP 1 (11 tests incl. the filed AC7 failure at line 983, corrected count from ISSUE-FIXER's ~10) -- restructure via a new @doc false, test-only synchronous seam on Executor that calls the existing private run_script/3 directly with no Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/Task.yield wrapper at all, precedented by this same file's existing build_script_error/3 test-only seam. No timeout value is read on this path, so the failure branch (handle_yield_result(nil, ...)) is structurally unreachable, not merely unlikely -- this is the run's own requested 'structurally verifiable, not statistical' shape, and directly addresses the filed failure by construction. GROUP 2 (11 tests, corrected count from ISSUE-FIXER's ~9, includes the 2 mixed tests' racing arm) -- new @tag :lua_wallclock_race (deliberately not reusing :wasm_hang's name, since ISSUE-FIXER's own registry lookup found LUA and WASM are same family but NOT same root cause -- no shared leaking resource on the lua side), wired into test/test_helper.exs's existing exclude: list and into a new, minimal, additive isolated subprocess in lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex mirroring run_wasm_hang_tests/0 line for line (same stream_and_capture/2 helper, same exit-code contract). The 2 mixed tests (656/887) get the tag applied whole-test (since each has one genuinely racing arm) but their own Group-1-shaped sub-calls are deliberately left unconverted rather than split into two tests, since tagging already isolates them from contention and splitting would fragment the single-test 'all N arms classify distinctly' property those tests exist to prove.

All four hard constraints addressed and stated satisfied in design section 3: (1) AC4 production semantics -- config/config.exs:17 never referenced, execute_with_manifest/2,3's existing bodies untouched, new seam is additive and test-only; (2) AC5 tag wiring -- test_helper.exs exclude: list gains one atom, letflow.check.test.ex gains one new sibling function + one new call site, zero lines of the existing run_wasm_hang_tests/0/stream_and_capture/2/collect/2 modified; (3) AC3 serial pass -- Group 1 no longer races at all (faster, not just safer), Group 2 excluded from plain `mix test` by the tag exactly as :wasm_hang already coexists with serial correctness today; (4) Group 2 detection power -- design section 2.2's table names the specific property each of the 11 tests proves, none of their assertions/workloads/timeout values change, only execution isolation.

DID touch the contested lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex, as instructed if AC5 forced it (it did -- :wasm_hang's own precedent requires isolation to be wired into this file). Kept it minimal and additive per instruction: one new private function (run_lua_wallclock_race_tests/0, shaped identically to run_wasm_hang_tests/0 with 3 substitutions: tag name, log/error text, nothing else) plus one new call site appended in run/1's success branch -- zero existing lines in that file touched. Flagged the merge-sequencing risk against WF03-ISS0418-20260902 explicitly in design section 2.3 for ORCH to sequence.

Validator can confirm the fix works WITHOUT reproducing the flake: Group 1's fix is a one-time structural/diff read (confirm the 11 call sites use the new no-Task seam, confirm the seam's own body contains no Task.yield/Task.Supervisor.async_nolink) -- this alone proves the filed failure's branch is unreachable, independent of host load. Group 2's fix is similarly a structural/diff read (tag applied to exactly the 11 listed tests, test_helper.exs excludes it, letflow.check.test.ex's new subprocess runs --only lua_wallclock_race) -- confirms contention is removed (isolated single-process subprocess, same low-contention environment :wasm_hang's own isolated run already uses today), not merely reduced. Design section 4 states this explicitly and gives TEST-RUNNER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR a concrete 4-step confirmation sequence, with the required scripts/test_parallel.sh 2x end-to-end run (ISS-0426 AC6's own literal text) listed as confirmatory rather than load-bearing evidence.

Two open questions left explicitly for ELIXIR-DEV/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR rather than silently resolved: OQ-1 (exact name/arity of the new synchronous seam -- behavior and precedent specified, ergonomics of the exact signature left open), OQ-2 (whether the 2 max_heap_words-limited Group 1 sites need a different synchronous mechanism than the nil-heap-words seam, since they currently route through run_with_heap_limit/5 rather than run_script/3 directly).

issues.description: Disagreement with ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis: the lua two-group enumeration was undercounted by 5 Group-1-shaped call sites (all in the REQ-154 instruction-budget describe block, executor_test.exs lines 253-321) that the diagnosis's own enumeration did not list (it started at line 452). Corrected counts used in this design: Group 1 = 11 tests (was ~10), Group 2 = 11 tests (was ~9, includes 2 tests' racing arm). Also found 2 tests (lines 656, 887) that are internally mixed -- one Group-1-shaped call and one genuinely-racing Group-2-shaped call in the same test body -- which the diagnosis did not flag as a structural wrinkle requiring its own narrower treatment (design section 2.4).

Found (not part of ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis scope): executor_test.exs:320's comment states config/test.exs sets a '200ms' default for lua_wallclock_timeout_ms; the actual configured value (config/test.exs:187) is 5000. Pre-existing drift in the test file's own comment, not a functional defect (no test in this file currently exercises the 2-arity fallback path that reads this config value) and not a disagreement with ISSUE-FIXER (which correctly cited 5000 elsewhere). Flagged in the design (section 1.2(c)) for ELIXIR-DEV to correct as a one-line drive-by fix while already touching that describe block.
